scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality, material, dimensional, and testing specifications for hexagon head coach screws (also referred to as hexagon head wood screws or lag screws) used in structural timber frameworks, general wood construction, electrical cross-arms, and other civil or railway engineering structures.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, dimensional parameters, shank diameters, and head dimensions must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Hexagon head coach screws are designated by the screw number (diameter sizing) and nominal length. Standard sizes covered in the code are Screw No. 10, 14, 18, 24, 28, and 32.

Specifies nominal, maximum, and minimum diameters for unthreaded shanks: Size 10 (Nom 4.88, Max 5.00, Min 4.72 mm); Size 14 (Nom 6.30, Max 6.43, Min 6.05 mm); Size 18 (Nom 7.72, Max 7.85, Min 7.47 mm); Size 24 (Nom 9.86, Max 9.98, Min 9.00 mm); Size 28 (Nom 11.20, Max 11.40, Min 11.02 mm); Size 32 (Nom 12.70, Max 12.83, Min 12.45 mm).
Tolerances are strictly specified as: js16 tolerance for head height k when the height is less than 4 mm (k < 4 mm); and js17 tolerance when the height is 10 mm or more (k >= 10 mm).
Steel coach screws must be manufactured from mild steel or low-carbon steel wire having physical and mechanical properties conforming to IS 451 : 1972.

Hexagon head coach screws shall be designated by name, screw number, length, standard number, and material. Example: A hexagon head coach screw of Screw No. 10, length 30 mm, made of steel: 'Coach Screw No. 10 x 30 IS : 1120 Steel'.
In regard to finish, inspection, acceptance, packaging, and marking, the coach screws must conform to the comprehensive requirements laid down in IS 451 : 1972.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1120 : 1975 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing quality requirements, material specifications, tolerances, and nominal dimensions for hexagon head coach screws (also referred to as hexagon head wood screws or lag screws). Maintained under the Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners Accessories Sectional Committee (PGD 31), the standard unifies structural wood fasteners used in heavy timber frameworks, overhead transmission cross-arms, and railway sleeper assemblies. It standardizes preferred screw sizes—No. 10, 14, 18, 24, 28, and 32—and specifies unthreaded shank diameters and strict tolerances (using the ISO system, such as js16 and js17). By referencing IS 451:1972 for technical supply and material guidelines, the standard ensures that coach screws provide optimal shear and pull-out resistance, preventing catastrophic wood structure collapse and supporting standardized on-site inspections.
